sources.entry: wrk2 - Issues requests on a fixed schedule and times each from when it was due, so server stalls reach the percentiles.

summary.one_liner: wrk2 is an HTTP benchmarking tool derived from wrk that sends requests at a constant target rate and records latency from when each request was scheduled, so server stalls show up in the percentiles.
summary.what_it_does: Runs HTTP load at a fixed total requests-per-second rate (set with -R/--rate, default 1000) spread across a configurable number of threads and connections. Latency is measured from the time each request was supposed to be sent, which corrects for Coordinated Omission. Per-run latency is stored in HdrHistogram rather than per-sample buffers, giving high-percentile accuracy. The --latency flag prints a percentile distribution, and --u_latency also prints an uncorrected distribution for comparison. An optional LuaJIT scripting API (init, request, response, done) customizes requests and reporting, with example scripts in scripts/. The README says measured latencies are accurate to roughly ±1 ms due to OS sleep behavior.
use_cases: measure HTTP server latency percentiles under constant load
benchmark a web service at a fixed requests-per-second rate
detect latency stalls that closed-loop load tools hide
compare corrected and uncorrected latency distributions
scripted HTTP load tests with Lua
notable: Constant-throughput load with latency timed from the scheduled send time, avoiding Coordinated Omission
Lossless latency recording with HdrHistogram, accurate into the high 9s percentiles
--u_latency flag reports an uncorrected distribution alongside the corrected one
Keeps wrk's Lua scripting API and its latency and requests stats objects
caveats: Latency accuracy is about ±1 ms due to OS sleep time behavior, per the README
Experimental/development mode according to the README
Calibration takes 10 seconds, so runs shorter than 10-20 seconds may not be informative
